page.title: 4 · Build the next season
page.description: Turn a friend’s first game into membership, then follow the clinch-or-fade renewal fork. Public facts cited; operational flows and uncited figures are illustrative.

sections.heading: Friend's ticket to member
text: One illustrative fan, Fan K., and one seat, Sec 312 at UBS Arena, over the 2026-27 season and into the next. The fan starts on a friend's transferred ticket, buys a single game, then a mini plan, then a membership. The bowl is coloured by *how Fan K. held each seat*, the cost panel compares what one game costs on each route, and the ledger shows the points program a membership opens.

Public facts (dates, giveaways, plans, member benefits, Isles Rewards rules) are cited from team pages. The systems and offer rules are an illustrative reconstruction, not a description of the Islanders', UBS Arena's or Ticketmaster's systems. Prices and point values are illustrative except the **$10 member parking** and the **15% member food and drink discount**.

bullets.text: **Sourced:** mobile-only entry and the 48-hour barcode release; GOAT USA Night (Dec 1) and the Schaefer bobblehead night (Feb 13); the 4-game Giveaway Plan; member parking, the 15% discount and other benefits; Isles Rewards rules.

bullets: **Illustrative:** Fan K., the seat moves, the offer rules, every ticket price, fee and point value.
Pick a path: **Offers follow the fan** runs both seasons; **No offer sent** shows the same guest with no follow-up.

routes.label: Single games
routes.tradeoff: Pick any night; full price and fees every time.

routes.label: Giveaway Plan
routes.tradeoff: 4 set nights: two bobbleheads, two gate giveaways.

routes.label: Half Season Member
routes.tradeoff: About half the home schedule; the perks around the seat do most of the saving.

panels.assumptions: Sourced: the $10 Emerald parking member rate and the 15% member food and drink discount (new for 2026-27). Everything else is illustrative: ticket prices, fees, the $30 non-member parking figure (illustrative; a 2024 fan newsletter cites $40+, and the team says lot prices vary by event) and a $40 food and drink spend, which becomes $34 at 15% off. Not team prices.

initial.note: Fan K. pays nothing yet: the friend paid for the October seat.
No ledger yet. Isles Rewards is for Full and Half Season Members, so a guest on a transferred ticket earns nothing.

steps.text: **Thu Oct 22, 2026 vs LAK.** Fan K.'s friend, a Half Season Member, transfers one seat in **Sec 312** to Fan K. The barcode appears in the app 48 hours before puck drop; entry at UBS Arena is mobile-only. Fan K. has spent nothing and has no plan.
steps.deltaText: Mobile-only entry and the 48-hour barcode release are published on the team's mobile ticket page.

map.note: Oct 22: Sec 312 on a friend's transferred ticket. Tier: guest. Capacities are an illustrative even split; Fan K. is illustrative.

steps.text: Fan K. scans in. Accepting the transfer meant creating an account, so for the first time the CRM holds a name, an email and one attended game for someone who never bought a ticket (illustrative flow).

map.note: Sec 312 scanned at the gate. The seat belongs to the friend's membership; the attendance now belongs to Fan K.'s new profile. Capacities are an illustrative even split; Fan K. is illustrative.

steps.text: An offer rule fires: *attended once, never bought*. The email names the next big night: **GOAT USA Night, Tue Dec 1 vs FLA**, with a Chuck the Goat ornament for the first 10,000 fans.
steps.deltaText: GOAT USA Night (Dec 1 vs FLA, ornament for the first 10,000) is on the 2026-27 promotional schedule. The offer rule is illustrative.

map.note: Nothing bought yet. The offer is aimed at one profile, not a section. Capacities are an illustrative even split; Fan K. is illustrative.

steps.text: Fan K. buys **one single-game ticket** for Dec 1. The friend's section is full that night, so the seat is in **Sec 309**, three sections over. Fan K. is now a buyer, paying full price, fees and parking (amounts illustrative).

map.note: Dec 1: a single-game ticket in Sec 309. Tier: single-game buyer. Capacities are an illustrative even split; Fan K. is illustrative.

cost.note: A single game: about $186 all in (illustrative).

steps.text: Two games attended. The next offer is the **Giveaway Plan**, four set nights with *two bobbleheads, two gate giveaways*. Fan K. buys it for the **Matthew Schaefer bobblehead night, Sat Feb 13 vs MIN**, and picks seats back in **Sec 312**.
steps.deltaText: The Giveaway Plan (Nov 27 WPG, Dec 1 FLA, Feb 13 MIN, Mar 7 PIT) is a published 2026-27 mini plan. How a plan bought mid-season is priced is not published, so the amounts here are illustrative.

map.note: Feb 13: Sec 312 again, now on Fan K.'s own Giveaway Plan. Tier: mini plan. Capacities are an illustrative even split; Fan K. is illustrative.

cost.note: Plan games cost about $168 each (illustrative): a lower ticket price and fees, the same parking and food.

steps.text: Spring renewal season. The rep's pitch is a comparison for the *same fan in the same section*. The ticket price falls a little; the bigger gaps are around the seat: **$10 member parking** and **15% off food and drink**.
steps.deltaText: Sourced member benefits: $10 Emerald parking per game and, new for 2026-27, 15% off concessions and bars for Full and Half Season Members. All other amounts are illustrative.

map.note: Two ways in so far: a single game in 309 and a plan seat in 312. Capacities are an illustrative even split; Fan K. is illustrative.

cost.note: Member: about $120 a game (illustrative), $66 less than a single game. Parking drops from $30 to $10; $40 of food costs $34.

steps.text: Fan K. signs up as a **Half Season Member** for 2027-28, in Sec 312, the seat that started as a friend's spare. Member benefits also include ticket exchange, playoff access and member events.

map.note: Sec 312 is now Fan K.'s membership seat. Tier: Half Season Member. Capacities are an illustrative even split; Fan K. is illustrative.

cost.note: Chosen route: Half Season Member (illustrative amounts, sourced parking rate and discount).

steps.text: Membership opens **Isles Rewards**. Fan K. first tries a personal email and the link fails: the program requires the *same email as the membership*. With the matching email, the ticket account links and points start.
steps.deltaText: Isles Rewards rules (members only, same email as the membership, points from attendance, Claim Now, content and in-game trivia, redemptions posted within 48 hours) are from the official program page. Point values are illustrative.

cells.what: Link with a different email: not matched

ledger.note: The failed link is the common support case: a second email address.

steps.text: Opening night of 2027-28. Attending at UBS Arena earns the most points, so the gate scan posts to the ledger. A daily **Claim Now** and a game watched from away add smaller amounts.

map.note: Fan K. in Sec 312 on opening night, now on the membership. Capacities are an illustrative even split; Fan K. is illustrative.

cells.what: Link with a different email: not matched

ledger.note: Attendance outweighs everything else in this illustrative ledger.

steps.text: During a stoppage, Fan K. answers the **live in-game trivia** in the app. Small points, but it keeps a member opening the app while in the seat.

cells.what: Link with a different email: not matched

ledger.note: 1,020 points: enough for the illustrative upgrade price of 800.

steps.text: Fan K. redeems points in the Marketplace for a **seat upgrade**. It posts to the ticket account within 48 hours, and for one November game Fan K. sits in **Sec 212**, down in the 200 level.

map.note: One game in Sec 212 on a rewards upgrade. Tier: rewards upgrade. Capacities are an illustrative even split; Fan K. is illustrative.

cells.what: Link with a different email: not matched

ledger.note: The burn is part of the design: a member who spends points has a reason to keep earning them.

steps.text: Two seasons on one bowl: a **single game** in 309, Sec 312 as a **guest**, then a **plan** seat, then a **membership** (the map keeps 312's latest colour), and one **upgrade** in 212. Each move followed one small offer triggered by what Fan K. had just done, and the first came before Fan K. had ever paid.

map.note: History: Sec 312 was held three ways (guest in Oct, Giveaway Plan in Feb, membership from 2027-28) and shows its latest tier; 309 was a single game and 212 one upgrade. The legend counts sections, not holds. Fan K. is illustrative.

cost.note: The member route wins on the perks around the seat, not mainly on the ticket price.

steps.text: **Without the offer rule.** If the CRM sends no *attended once, never bought* offer, Fan K. stays a one-time guest: a name, an email and one scan on file. The next night in Sec 312 is the friend's seat again, and the profile goes cold (illustrative).

map.note: Only the Oct 22 guest seat, ever. Fan K. is illustrative.

sections.heading: Clinch or fade
text: In mid-March nobody knows whether the playoff games exist, yet members must be invoiced, presales staged and giveaways sourced. Playoff ticketing is **conditional inventory**: it is built and priced before the schedule is real, and the elimination branch needs as much planning as the clinch.

Two paths share one board. **Eliminated** is what actually happened to the 2025-26 Islanders (out on Apr 12, 2026). **Clinch** replays the April 2024 playbook (home Games 3 and 4 against Carolina). Both end at the 2026-27 renewal, where All-Star 2027 priority is the lever.
bullets: **Sourced:** 2024 Round 1 dates and Apr 20 on-sale ([NHL.com](https://nhl.com/islanders/news/islanders-hurricanes-first-round-schedule-announced-2024)); rally towels, commemorative ticket and doors 90 minutes early ([The Hockey News](https://thehockeynews.com/nhl/new-york-islanders/game-day/new-york-islanders-playoffs-ubs-arena-hurricanes-game-three)); elimination Apr 12, 2026 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_New_York_Islanders_season)); All-Star 2027 member priority and waitlist ([NHL.com](https://www.nhl.com/islanders/fans/all-star)); $100 membership deposit, published for 2025-26 ([NHL.com](https://www.nhl.com/islanders/tickets/2025-26-deposits)).
**Pattern, not Islanders policy:** charge at clinch or on a date, and credits for unplayed games, follow the [Oilers' 2026 FAQ](https://www.nhl.com/oilers/tickets/season-seat-holders/renewal-faq).
**Illustrative:** member accounts, prices, risk reasons, the All-Star allocation split, every funnel count and all sell-through. Seat capacities are an even split of 17,250 over 80 sections.

panels.title: UBS Arena · playoff, then All-Star inventory

initial.note: Playoff Round 1 home game. Capacities: illustrative even split of 17,250 over 80 sections.
Opens once the playoff question is settled (counts illustrative).

steps.text: **Mid-March 2026: in the hunt.** The standings move nightly, so ticket ops builds playoff inventory for home games that may never exist. Every section is *held* for a conditional Round 1 home game, and nothing is on sale yet.

map.note: Every seat held for a Round 1 home game that is not yet scheduled.

ledger.note: Illustrative member accounts; no real fans.

steps.text: **Pre-build both branches.** Member playoff invoices are queued to charge *at clinch or on a fixed date, whichever comes first* (the Oilers published this rule for 2026). Marketing drafts the presale email *and* the credit email, and promotions gets a rally-towel quote, because towels can be made in days and bobbleheads cannot.

ledger.note: Charge rule follows the Oilers' 2026 pattern; prices illustrative.

steps.deltaText: Oilers 2026: first playoff payment at clinch or by a set date; unplayed games become credit or refund.

deltaLinks.label: NHL.com Oilers: renewal and 2026 playoffs FAQ

steps.text: **Clinch (the branch that did not happen in 2026).** The magic number hits zero. Billing charges the first home game, and the schedule fixes the dates. The playbook is April 2024: Round 1 against Carolina, home Games 3 and 4 at UBS Arena on Apr 25 and 27.

map.note: Dates fixed: two Round 1 home games (2024 pattern: Apr 25 and 27). Seats still held for members.

ledger.note: G4 charges only if G4 is played. Prices illustrative.

steps.deltaText: 2024: Islanders vs Hurricanes, home Games 3 and 4 on Apr 25 and 27, 2024.

steps.text: **Member presale.** Members get first access, so the lower bowl and the clubs go first while the 300 level barely moves. The held hatch turns into real sales section by section.

map.note: Member presale: clubs gone, 100 level near 90%, 300 level about 12% (illustrative).

steps.deltaText: Playoff Access is a listed member benefit (member benefits page).

steps.text: **Public on-sale, five days out.** In 2024 single-game tickets went on sale Apr 20 for an Apr 25 Game 3. The bowl fills from the bottom up, and the sold count becomes the towel order: one per seat, plus a buffer.

map.note: Public on-sale: 100 level sold out, 300 level about 86% (illustrative).

ledger.note: 2024 Game 3 precedent: rally towels and a commemorative ticket for all fans, doors 90 minutes early.

steps.deltaText: Single-game tickets for 2024 Games 3 and 4 went on sale Apr 20, 2024.

steps.text: **Game night.** Every seat is sold and every seat gets a rally towel. This is the 2024 precedent: towels and a commemorative ticket for all fans, The Park with contests, doors 90 minutes early. Game 4 went to double overtime and the Islanders won 3-2.

map.note: Sold out (illustrative full house). 2024: rally towels for all fans.

steps.deltaText: 2024 Game 3 at UBS Arena: rally towels, commemorative ticket, doors 90 minutes early.

deltaLinks.label: The Hockey News: Game 3 at UBS Arena

steps.text: **The date trigger fires first.** No clinch yet, but the fixed charge date arrives, so the first playoff payment is taken anyway. This is the trap the pre-built credit email exists for.

ledger.note: Charged on the date rule before the season is decided (illustrative).

steps.text: **Apr 12, 2026: eliminated.** This is what actually happened: a second straight playoff miss for a 43-34-5 team. The conditional inventory is released and the bowl empties. Not one playoff seat was ever sold. Source: [Wikipedia: 2025-26 Islanders season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_New_York_Islanders_season) · [Yardbarker: Islanders eliminated](https://www.yardbarker.com/nhl/articles/islanders_officially_eliminated_from_2026_stanley_cup_playoff_contention/s1_16958_43721010).

map.note: Conditional inventory released: no Round 1 home game.

steps.text: **Unplayed games become credits.** Each charged payment turns into an account credit for next season, refundable on request (the Oilers' published pattern). The credit email that was drafted in March goes out the same day. Source: [NHL.com Oilers: renewal and 2026 playoffs FAQ](https://www.nhl.com/oilers/tickets/season-seat-holders/renewal-faq).

ledger.note: Credit or refund election per account (illustrative).

steps.text: **The same table becomes the rep queue.** Sorted by churn risk: newer members churn more, and a member who asked for a refund after a losing season is the first call. Flag *transferred* seats before calling, because a member whose family uses the seats is not absent. Source: [Chief Marketer: LA Kings churn modelling](https://www.chiefmarketer.com/la-kings-turn-to-modeling-to-ice-churn/).

map.note: Pulsed: seats of the four accounts in the rep queue.

ledger.note: Risk order and reasons illustrative; LA Kings model churn from about 10 games in.

steps.text: **Both branches meet at renewal.** The 2026-27 renewal carries one line no rival can match: Full and Half Season Members get *guaranteed access to buy tickets* (subject to availability) for the 2027 All-Star Weekend at UBS Arena. Others joined a waitlist; the team's 2025-26 deposit page asked $100 for priority access to a new membership (the 2026-27 amount is not confirmed).

map.note: All-Star access plan by section (allocation illustrative; the league's split is not published).

ledger.note: Order of access illustrative except member priority, which is published.

steps.deltaText: Full and Half Season Members get guaranteed access to buy All-Star 2027 tickets, subject to availability; a waitlist opened for others (The Hockey News); $100 deposit for membership priority was published for 2025-26.

steps.text: **All-Star 2027 closes the loop.** Feb 5-6, 2027: a 3-on-3 round robin with fan voting. Waitlist fans are offered the seats that remain, and the ones who buy get a membership pitch. The event is a one-time acquisition window, so the last funnel stage is the one that matters next season.

map.note: All-Star sell-through (illustrative). Pulsed: waitlist sections.

funnel.note: Converted: waitlist buyers who took a 2026-27 membership (illustrative).

steps.deltaText: 2027 NHL All-Star Weekend at UBS Arena, Feb 5-6, 2027; 3-on-3 round robin with fan voting.
